tagline.text: The island's only waterfall, about 15 m tall in the northern Siargao jungle

location.label: Location
location.text: Santa Monica (formerly Sapao), northern Siargao Island, Surigao del Norte

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: March–October for relatively clear weather (the falls flow fullest June–November)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~1,200 (motorbike rental, entrance fee and snacks, per person)

children.text: Taktak Falls is the only waterfall on Siargao Island, in Santa Monica in the north. A pool you can swim in lies beneath the roughly 15 m drop, and well-built concrete paths make it an easy stop. It is quite far from General Luna, so it works best combined with a drive around the north.

Taktak Falls lies inland in Santa Monica (formerly called Sapao) in northern Siargao Island. Because Siargao is famous for surfing and beaches and this is practically its only waterfall, it is often introduced as "the island's only waterfall." Travel accounts differ slightly on the height, but it is generally described as around
. The name is said to come from a Visayan word meaning "to fall" or "to drip."

Below the falls, natural pools and some man-made sections sit side by side, and a short walk down a concrete path from the entrance hut brings you to the water. The deep, shaded water is cool and pleasant on a hot day, but in the rainy season, when the flow is heavy, it tends to turn brown and murky. Some visitors were disappointed after expecting clear blue-green water, so it is best to keep your expectations modest.
The biggest factor is distance. It is said to take about
1 hour 30 minutes
by motorbike from General Luna and about
20 minutes

from Pacifico in the north. For that reason, most people do not come only for the falls but make a day of it together with the northern surf town of Pacifico, Alegria Beach and the Magpupungko rock pools. If time is short, you might consider the beaches and island tours in the south before the falls. For first-time visitors, plan your day carefully. You usually need only
30 minutes–1 hour

at the falls, and most trip reports mention about an hour, so the round trip will take more than half your day. If you are not comfortable riding a motorbike, rather than spending a whole day from General Luna, it is easier to move to the north and stay in Pacifico. Even if the falls fall short of your hopes, the palm-lined road and the beaches on the way make up for it, so think of the falls as one stop on a scenic drive. Review sites such as Tripadvisor also carry opinions that the falls are overhyped, so keep that in mind.

This is not a heavily developed tourist site. You sign a visitor log at the entrance and pay a small fee, and the only facilities are changing rooms, restrooms and a small shop. There are no lifeguards, so you are responsible for your own safety in the water. In recent years, some visitors feel that added concrete work has reduced the natural feel, while others say the easier paths make the falls accessible to everyone.
Siargao is centered on beaches and surf breaks, so waterfalls are rare. Taktak Falls is a single drop of about
set against the jungle, offering a different kind of scenery. It is a good choice when you want a freshwater swim after days by the sea.

blocks.title: A swimming pool beneath the falls

children.text: Below the cascade is a deep, shaded pool that is good for swimming. Some parts are shallow with large boulders, so the depth varies from spot to spot. When you first get in, go slowly and check that your feet can touch the bottom.

The path from the entrance toward the falls is mostly paved with concrete and takes only a few minutes to walk. You can go in sandals without hiking gear, and children and older travelers will not find it hard if they take their time. Mossy steps are slippery, so water shoes are a good idea.

You may see people jumping into the water from a branch stretching out over the pool, and local children sometimes show visitors the spot. Not every part of the pool is safe, however, so do not jump until you have checked the depth yourself.
A paved path on the left leads to the top of the falls, so you can enjoy both the view from above and the view looking up from below. The rocks are often wet, so stay away from the edge.

blocks.title: A stop on a northern drive

children.text: The ride itself is part of the experience. Along palm-lined roads and quiet villages you see the slow pace of northern Siargao. Time at the falls is short at about
30 minutes–1 hour
, so it is best seen as a rest stop along the way.

blocks.title: The entrance hut and small shop

children.text: The entrance hut sits just above the falls and is where you leave your visit record. A small shop nearby sells drinks and snacks, and its tables are a good place to rest. Using a table may cost an extra fee, so check before you sit.

items.title: Day trip from General Luna
items.subtitle: A northern drive and a swim at the falls

children.text: Set out from General Luna by motorbike or rental car. Before leaving, pack cash, water, a towel and a change of clothes, and fill the tank.
Ride north along the main road, take a break once, and check the location of the falls entrance on a map app. The signs near the end can be confusing, so take your time.
Arrive at Taktak Falls, sign the visitor log at the entrance and pay the entrance and parking fees. Go early when few people are around and you may have the falls almost to yourself.
Walk down the concrete path, look around the falls and swim. Check the depth before getting in.
Change out of wet clothes and continue to Pacifico or Alegria Beach for lunch.
Head back toward General Luna before dark. The northern road has almost no streetlights.
Times are for a motorbike and can vary a lot with road conditions and weather. Leaving early is the best precaution.

items.title: Half day from Del Carmen
items.subtitle: Starting from the side near the airport

children.text: Leave from a hotel in Del Carmen town or near the airport. From here the ride is said to take roughly
40–60 minutes
by motorbike.
Arrive at the falls, finish the entry procedure and walk down the path.
Swim and take photos. If the water is brown or high, do not get in and just enjoy the view.
On the way back, stop at northern sights such as the Maasin River palm viewpoint and return to Del Carmen.

items.title: From the airport to the falls

children.text: Siargao Airport is in Del Carmen on the west side of the island. From Del Carmen to the falls it is about
40–60 minutes
by motorbike.
From General Luna it is about 54 km, roughly
1 hour 30 minutes
by motorbike. A motorbike rental costs about
per day.
There is almost no public transport or group tour, so renting a motorbike or car, or hiring a tricycle, is the usual way.

If you do not have an international driving license or do not feel safe on a motorbike, arranging a car with a driver through your accommodation or a tour operator is safer. Because of the distance, the fare is higher than for ordinary town trips, so negotiate and confirm it first.
The falls flow fullest in the rainy season, June–November, but the water gets murky and the paths turn slippery. After several days of rain, the paths near the falls can turn to mud.

The time when the water is clearer and getting around by motorbike is easier is the relatively clear March–October period, and some guides say April–September is safest. Whatever the season, avoid swimming right after rain.

There is almost no accommodation near the falls, so most people stay in General Luna, Del Carmen or Pacifico in the north and visit on a day trip. The entrance has only a small shop selling drinks and snacks, so it is better to have lunch at a village eatery on the way or in the Pacifico and Alegria area.
Restaurants and convenience stores are far apart on the northern road, so bring water, snacks and cash in advance. There are mosquitoes, so insect repellent is also handy.

The key to choosing where to stay is travel time. Staying in Pacifico in the north puts you close to the falls with a surf-town atmosphere, but options are limited. General Luna has the most hotels and restaurants and is the most convenient, but the falls are far. Del Carmen, where the airport is, is convenient for fitting the falls in on your arrival or departure day. Before booking, check travel times on a map app, and in the rainy season keep your plans flexible according to the weather forecast.
Pay the entrance and parking fees in cash. Bring plenty of small change.
Bring swimwear, water shoes, a towel and a change of clothes. The changing rooms are basic.
Early morning (7–9 AM) or late afternoon is quiet.
Save the location on Google Maps beforehand and watch for signs so you do not get lost. Some people miss the sign at the last fork.
The falls are far for a trip of their own, so combine them with Pacifico, Alegria Beach and the Magpupungko rock pools.
Magpupungko rock pools can be visited only at certain times depending on the tide, so check a tide chart when planning.
Return before dark. The northern road is very dark at night.
When coming from General Luna, fill up the tank before leaving. Gas stations are rare on the northern road.
On rainy days, the danger at the falls and the slipperiness of the road both increase, so it is wise to postpone to another day.
Right after rain the water rises, turns brown and carries a flash-flood risk, so do not swim. Always check the depth before jumping in.
Mossy steps and rocks are very slippery. Wear water shoes and hold the railings.
There are no lifeguards, so do not swim alone and watch children closely.
The depth varies from spot to spot for diving. Do not jump in until you have checked it yourself.
On long motorbike rides, wear a helmet and check your license and insurance. Roads are slippery after rain.
Fees and opening hours can change, so check the latest announcements.
